content: In Zechariah, on what animal does the coming King ride?
explanation: Jesus fulfilled this on Palm Sunday. “humble and riding on a donkey, on a colt, the foal of a donkey.” (Zechariah 9:9, BSB)

content: In Zechariah, “Not by might nor by power, but by My…”
explanation: God's work is done His way. “Not by might nor by power, but by My Spirit, says the LORD of Hosts.” (Zechariah 4:6, BSB)

content: In Zechariah's vision of Jerusalem, who will fill the streets playing?
explanation: Peace will return to the city. “And the streets of the city will be filled with boys and girls playing there.” (Zechariah 8:5, BSB)

content: In Zechariah, how is the King coming to Zion described?
explanation: He is also righteous and victorious. “See, your King comes to you, righteous and victorious, humble and riding on a donkey” (Zechariah 9:9, BSB)

content: In Zechariah, God asks who has despised the day of what?
explanation: Small beginnings matter to God. “For who has despised the day of small things?” (Zechariah 4:10, BSB)

content: In Zechariah's vision, who will sit along Jerusalem's streets again?
explanation: Each with a staff because of age. “Old men and old women will again sit along the streets of Jerusalem” (Zechariah 8:4, BSB)

content: In Zechariah, what happens when the Shepherd is struck?
explanation: Jesus quoted this before His arrest. “Strike the Shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered” (Zechariah 13:7, BSB)

content: In Zechariah, to whom was the word “Not by might nor by power” given?
explanation: He led the temple rebuilding. “This is the word of the LORD to Zerubbabel” (Zechariah 4:6, BSB)

content: Who was the prophet Zechariah's father?
explanation: His grandfather was Iddo. “the word of the LORD came to the prophet Zechariah son of Berechiah, the son of Iddo” (Zechariah 1:1, BSB)

content: In Zechariah, what will the seven eyes of the LORD rejoice to see in Zerubbabel's hand?
explanation: The temple would be finished. “will rejoice when they see the plumb line in the hand of Zerubbabel.” (Zechariah 4:10, BSB)
